evidence.explanation: Advises against aggressive orthopaedic surgery; the sentence continues past a line break in the cached full text so only the verifiable span is quoted.

treatments/8.description: No specific or disease-modifying treatment exists. Care is directed at quality of life, infection control and symptom relief; aggressive orthopaedic intervention for contractures is generally not recommended because poor general status and low survival compromise surgical outcomes.

evidence.snippet: No evidence of a recognised metabolic disorder was found in any of the six infants
evidence.explanation: The primary series describes a renal tubulopathy phenotype and reports no haematological marrow-failure disorder, contradicting the ICD-11 parentage.

open_questions/0.rationale: The ICD-11 Foundation entity icd11f:235762608 defines FID as "the association of Fanconi anaemia, ichthyosis, musculo-skeletal anomalies, jaundice, and diarrhoea" and places it under Fanconi anaemia. The primary description (PMID:2206896), its MeSH synonym, and MONDO all use "Fanconi syndrome" in the renal proximal-tubulopathy sense; MONDO:0022948 is classified under MONDO:0001083 Fanconi renotubular syndrome. Nothing in the primary literature describes bone marrow failure, pancytopenia, chromosome breakage or cancer predisposition in these infants, and the molecular aetiology — biallelic VPS33B/VIPAS39 loss disrupting apical trafficking — has no relationship to the Fanconi anaemia DNA interstrand-crosslink repair pathway. The ICD-11 placement appears to be a homonym error between two unrelated Fanconi eponyms, and it propagates into any downstream system that inherits ICD-11 parentage. dismech records the mapping as a narrow match - the ICD-11 definition delimits the arthrogryposis-poor FID end of this entry's ARC spectrum - while flagging the parentage as incorrect.

evidence.snippet: The association of Fanconi syndrome, ichthyosis, dysmorphism, jaundice, and diarrhoea has previously been reported as a separate syndrome: our observations indicate that it is part of the ARC spectrum.
evidence.explanation: The phenotypic, pre-molecular basis on which FID was subsumed into the ARC spectrum — strong, but not genotype-confirmed for the FID probands themselves.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in VIPAR accounted for all cases of classical ARC in whom mutations in and linkage to VPS33B were excluded.
evidence.explanation: Evidence bearing on whether a third locus is likely: VIPAS39 closed the residual gap in classical ARC, arguing against an unidentified FID locus.

open_questions/1.rationale: The 1990 FID series predates the identification of VPS33B (2004) and VIPAS39 (2010), so no proband from that series has a confirmed genotype. The assignment of FID to the ARC spectrum rests on the phenotypic argument made by Eastham and colleagues in 2001 (PMID:11668108) plus the subsequent demonstration that VPS33B-null patients can lack arthrogryposis (PMID:16492441). That argument is strong but is not the same as molecular proof for these specific families. Because the assignment determines whether FID should be retired as an independent entity or retained as a distinct locus, the gap is worth stating explicitly rather than papering over.

evidence.snippet: corroborate its role in the specialized delivery of cargo in different cell types
evidence.explanation: Frames CHEVI as a general cargo-delivery mechanism operating across cell types, which is the recurrence criterion a dismech mechanism module requires.

open_questions/2.rationale: The mechanism curated here — CHEVI/RAB11A-dependent apical recycling failure producing simultaneous epithelial polarity loss and defective biogenesis of two lysosome-related organelles (lamellar body, platelet alpha-granule) — is shared across ARC syndrome, this FID presentation, and the allelic ARKID syndrome, and is conceptually adjacent to other lysosome-related-organelle disorders (Hermansky-Pudlak, Chediak-Higashi). No existing dismech module covers it: the `epithelial_barrier_dysfunction` and `intestinal_barrier_dysfunction` modules model allergic and inflammatory barrier loss, not a constitutive trafficking lesion. No `conforms_to` edge is asserted in this entry for that reason. If ARC syndrome and ARKID are curated as separate entries, a shared module becomes worthwhile.

evidence.snippet: The association of Fanconi syndrome, ichthyosis, dysmorphism, jaundice, and diarrhoea has previously been reported as a separate syndrome: our observations indicate that it is part of the ARC spectrum.
evidence.explanation: The published statement that the two labels denote one entity, which is what MONDO has not yet reflected in its class hierarchy.

open_questions/3.rationale: MONDO:0022948 is an unreconciled legacy class. It has no textual definition, no gene association, and no OMIM xref - only Genetic and Rare Diseases Information Center, MEDGEN, MeSH and UMLS cross-references - and it is classified under MONDO:0001083 Fanconi renotubular syndrome. By contrast MONDO:0017123 has an Orphanet-sourced definition, an OMIMPS xref, and two gene-defined children (MONDO:0008822 VPS33B, MONDO:0013255 VIPAS39). The primary literature closed this gap in 2001: PMID:11668108 concluded that the Fanconi syndrome-ichthyosis-dysmorphism-jaundice-diarrhoea association "is part of the ARC spectrum", and the molecular basis was established in 2004 and 2010. So the two MONDO classes denote the same patients, one of them without any mechanistic grounding. dismech anchors on MONDO:0017123 and records MONDO:0022948 as a close match; the ontology-side fix is out of scope here but worth filing upstream.

evidence.snippet: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are essential enzymes responsible for charging amino acids onto cognate tRNAs during protein synthesis.
evidence.explanation: States the normal function of the affected enzyme class.

evidence.snippet: Mutants V133F and Y330C showed the most significant growth defect and decreased HARS abundance in cells.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates allele-specific reduction in protein abundance.

evidence.snippet: Expression of this variant in patient cells resulted in reduced aminoacylation activity in extracts obtained from dermal fibroblasts, without compromising overall protein synthesis.
evidence.explanation: Confirms reduced enzymatic activity in patient cells, while showing bulk protein synthesis was preserved — a constraint on any downstream model.

steps/1.description: HARS1 is the cytoplasmic aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase that ligates histidine to its cognate tRNA. The CMT2W alleles — V133F, V155G, Y330C and S356N — all sit in the catalytic domain. Their consequences at the protein level are not uniform: V133F and Y330C reduce HARS1 abundance in cells and V133F is thermally destabilized in vitro (rescued by tRNA), while V155G and S356N retain enough activity to mischarge. This heterogeneity is the reason the downstream mechanism is curated as competing hypotheses rather than a single chain.

evidence.snippet: Mullen et al. generate new models of pathogenic, dominant HARS1 mutations and show that they increase eIF2α phosphorylation and decrease protein translation in neurons.
evidence.explanation: Secondary framing only. This record's `publication_types` include "Comment" and it generated no model-organism data - the attribution to Mullen et al. is restored to the quote so that is visible. The primary result is cited directly in the item below.

evidence.snippet: The expression of CMT-HARS1 mutations led to attenuation of protein synthesis and increased phosphorylation of eIF2α in PC12 cells and was accompanied by impaired neurite and axon outgrowth in both models.
evidence.explanation: The primary experimental result behind the translational-stress arm, cited directly rather than through the commentary above.

evidence.snippet: Mistranslating V155G and S356N mutants lead to accumulation of insoluble proteins, which was rescued by histidine.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the proteotoxic arm for the mistranslating alleles, and its histidine-dependence.

steps/2.description: The step between a partly defective synthetase and a dying axon is the least settled part of this disease, and the evidence supports more than one route. Neuronal models of dominant HARS1 alleles show increased eIF2-alpha phosphorylation with decreased protein translation, the integrated stress response signature. Separately, mischarging alleles produce insoluble protein accumulation, and at least one severe allele forms HARS1 protein aggregates directly. These are curated as competing hypotheses below; the node is marked PROVISIONAL because which route dominates in human peripheral nerve is unknown.

evidence.snippet: Expression of D364Y mutant proteins inhibited process formation whereas expression of wild type proteins possessed the normal differentiation ability to grow processes.
evidence.explanation: Direct demonstration that a mutant HARS1 allele blocks neuronal process formation.

evidence.snippet: Type 2 CMT (CMT2) disease is a neuropathy with blunted or disrupted neuronal morphological differentiation phenotypes including process formation of peripheral neuronal axons.
evidence.explanation: Frames impaired process formation as the defining cellular lesion of CMT2.

steps/3.description: The cellular readout is failure of neuronal process formation and, in patients, degeneration of the longest peripheral axons. In neuronal cells the D364Y patient allele forms small HARS1 aggregates and inhibits process formation, whereas wild-type protein distributes through the cell body and supports normal differentiation. In patients this manifests as an axonal neuropathy; demyelination is not the primary lesion in CMT2 and is rarely seen early.

evidence.snippet: Inherited peripheral neuropathies are a genetically heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by distal muscle weakness and sensory loss.
evidence.explanation: Class-level framing from the four-family series that defined CMT2W, quoted in full rather than clipped so its scope is visible: it describes inherited peripheral neuropathies generally, not CMT2W specifically. The CMT2W-specific statement is carried by the PMID:36164730 item alongside it.

evidence.snippet: HARS is specifically associated with Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease type 2 W (CMT2W), an autosomal dominant axonal-form subtype of CMT. Most patients present with gait difficulties, foot deformities and distal sensory impairments (7).
evidence.explanation: Presenting features across the reported CMT2W patients.

steps/4.description: Clinically the disorder is a Charcot-Marie-Tooth phenotype affecting sensory as well as motor nerves, with distal muscle weakness and wasting. Because the longest axons fail first, deficits begin distally in the feet and progress proximally. Onset can be late: one reported V133F patient presented at 49 years.

evidence.snippet: In histidyl-tRNA synthetase (HARS), autosomal dominant mutations V133F, V155G, Y330C and S356N in the HARS catalytic domain cause Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 W (CMT2W), while tRNA-binding domain mutation Y454S causes recessive Usher syndrome type IIIB.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the domain-to-disease and domain-to-inheritance correspondence within HARS1.

evidence.snippet: V133F proteins displayed reduced thermal stability in vitro, which was rescued by tRNA.
evidence.explanation: Characterizes the biophysical defect of one allele and its tRNA-dependent stabilization.

evidence.snippet: All mutations cause a loss of function in yeast complementation assays, and p.Asp364Tyr is dominantly neurotoxic in a Caenorhabditis elegans model.
evidence.explanation: Establishes loss of function across the four-family allele set and dominant neurotoxicity for p.Asp364Tyr in an animal model.

genes/0.notes: HARS1 (5q31.3) encodes cytoplasmic histidyl-tRNA synthetase. Domain location predicts both the disease and its inheritance mode: catalytic-domain missense alleles cause dominant CMT2W, while the tRNA-binding domain allele Y454S causes recessive Usher syndrome type IIIB. The reported CMT2W alleles span at least V133F, V155G, Y330C, S356N and, from a four-family linkage-plus-exome study, p.Thr132Ile, p.Pro134His, p.Asp175Glu and p.Asp364Tyr. Note that p.Asp364Tyr — the allele whose aggregation behaviour was later characterised in neuronal cells — is a patient allele from that series, not a laboratory construct, and it was separately shown to be dominantly neurotoxic in C. elegans. Allele-specific biochemistry differs within CMT2W itself — some alleles mistranslate, others reduce protein abundance — which is why treatment inferences must be made per allele rather than per gene.

evidence.snippet: The expression of CMT-HARS1 mutations led to attenuation of protein synthesis and increased phosphorylation of eIF2α in PC12 cells and was accompanied by impaired neurite and axon outgrowth in both models.
evidence.explanation: The primary experimental result: integrated-stress-response activation with reduced translation, in PC12 neurites and zebrafish axons. Cited directly rather than through the commentary that summarizes it.

evidence.snippet: The mutant proteins also formed heterodimers with wild-type HARS1, raising the possibility that CMT-HARS1 mutations cause disease through a dominant-negative mechanism.
evidence.explanation: The heterodimer result is the physical basis for the dominant-negative reading, and it is marked PARTIAL because the authors themselves state it only "raises the possibility" - the hypothesis is CANONICAL by convergence across the ARS neuropathies, not because this experiment settles it.

evidence.snippet: These results are consistent with a dominant-negative mechanism of ARS-mediated peripheral neuropathy.
evidence.explanation: Secondary framing only. This record's `publication_types` include "Comment"; it is a one-paragraph commentary on the Mullen et al. study cited above, so it is tagged OTHER rather than MODEL_ORGANISM - it generated no model-organism data of its own. Retained because it states the generalization to the ARS neuropathies as a class, which the primary paper does not.

hypotheses/0.description: Mutant HARS1 acts dominant-negatively on the wild-type enzyme, reducing effective aminoacylation and triggering the integrated stress response. Neuronal models of dominant HARS1 alleles show increased eIF2-alpha phosphorylation and decreased protein translation, and this is the model most often generalized across the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase neuropathies.

evidence.snippet: We show mistranslation of histidine to glutamine and threonine in V155G and S356N but not Y330C mutants in yeast.
evidence.explanation: Establishes mistranslation for two alleles and its absence for a third, the basis for this being an alternative rather than universal model.

evidence.snippet: Mistranslating V155G and S356N mutants lead to accumulation of insoluble proteins, which was rescued by histidine.
evidence.explanation: Links mistranslation to proteotoxic accumulation and shows it is histidine-reversible.

hypotheses/1.description: Some CMT2W alleles do not simply lose activity — they mischarge. V155G and S356N mistranslate histidine to glutamine and threonine, and the resulting aberrant proteins accumulate as an insoluble fraction. On this model the proximate injury is proteotoxic rather than a translation-rate deficit, and the two are distinguishable experimentally because mistranslation-driven aggregation is rescued by histidine while abundance-limited alleles are made worse by it. Notably Y330C, also a CMT2W allele, did not mistranslate, so this model cannot be the whole story for the gene.

evidence.snippet: Here we show that in neuronal N1E-115 cells, a severe Asp364-to-Tyr (D364Y) mutation of HARS1 leads to formation of small aggregates of HARS1 proteins; in contrast, wild type proteins are distributed throughout cell bodies.
evidence.explanation: Direct demonstration that the mutant enzyme itself aggregates in neuronal cells.

hypotheses/2.description: A third route, shown for the D364Y patient allele: mutant HARS1 itself forms small intracellular aggregates rather than distributing through the cell body, and this coincides with failure of neuronal process outgrowth. Here the mutant protein is the aggregating species, distinguishing this from the mistranslation model in which the aggregating species is the mistranslated proteome.

open_questions/0.rationale: This is the most clinically consequential open question in CMT2W and it is curated as a hazard rather than a therapeutic lead. Histidine rescued the insoluble-protein accumulation caused by the mistranslating alleles V155G and S356N. For V133F and Y330C — the alleles with reduced HARS1 abundance — histidine did the opposite: it led to insoluble protein aggregation and further reduced viability, which the authors describe explicitly as histidine toxicity. A supplement that is intuitively harmless, and available without prescription, is therefore predicted to worsen a subset of patients. Nothing yet establishes that the yeast-model direction predicts the human direction, nor whether an untested allele can be assigned to the rescue or toxicity group in advance.

open_questions/1.rationale: Evidence exists in models; translational validity is the open question, which is what distinguishes this from a generic knowledge gap. Every mechanistic step in this entry comes from yeast complementation, neuronal cell lines or animal models: the mistranslation and histidine-response work is yeast, the eIF2-alpha and translation data are neuronal models, the aggregation and valproate result is an N1E-115 cell line. The only human cellular measurement is reduced aminoacylation in patient fibroblast extracts — and that same experiment found overall protein synthesis was not compromised, which sits awkwardly with the translation-attenuation model. No human nerve tissue from a CMT2W patient has been examined for any of these mechanisms. The entry's central node is PROVISIONAL for this reason as much as for the allele heterogeneity.

open_questions/2.rationale: The defining puzzle of the whole aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase neuropathy family, and the reason the central node here is PROVISIONAL. Every cell needs charged histidyl-tRNA, yet the phenotype falls on the longest peripheral axons. A simple translation-insufficiency account is further constrained by the finding that a patient variant reduced aminoacylation activity in fibroblast extracts without compromising overall protein synthesis, which suggests the disease-relevant deficit is not bulk translation capacity. The reporting authors state directly that further studies are needed to explain the neuronal specificity. Candidate explanations — a moonlighting function of the synthetase, the extreme translational and transport demands of a long axon, or a neuron-specific sensitivity to the integrated stress response — are not distinguished by current data.

evidence.snippet: HOXD13, the most 5' gene of the HOXD cluster, encodes a homeodomain transcription factor with important functions in limb patterning and growth.
evidence.explanation: Establishes HOXD13's role in limb patterning.

evidence.snippet: Heterozygous mutations of human HOXD13, encoding polyalanine expansions or frameshifts, are believed to act by dominant negative or haploinsufficiency mechanisms and are predominantly associated with synpolydactyly phenotypes.
evidence.explanation: Contrasts the BDE allele class with the synpolydactyly allele class of the same gene.

evidence.snippet: the Ile314Leu mutation (which resides at the 47th position of the homeodomain) exhibited increased affinity for a target containing the core recognition sequence 5'-TTAC-3' but decreased affinity for a 5'-TTAT-3' target
evidence.explanation: Shows the missense allele rebalances rather than abolishes target-site selection.

evidence.snippet: So far, only two missense HOXD13 substitutions (p.S308C and p.I314L), localized within the homeodomain of the HOXD13 transcription factor, as well as a single nonsense mutation (p.E181X) were associated with BDE.
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the BDE-associated HOXD13 allele set before the reported case.

steps/1.description: HOXD13, the most 5' gene of the HOXD cluster, encodes a homeodomain transcription factor that patterns the autopod. The alleles associated with isolated BDE are of two kinds: homeodomain missense substitutions, of which Ile314Leu at homeodomain position 47 has been shown to shift DNA-binding preference between related target sequences rather than abolish it, and truncating nonsense alleles such as p.E181X and p.R274X. Both classes are distinct from the polyalanine expansions and frameshifts that dominate the HOXD13 mutation spectrum and cause synpolydactyly — the same gene reaches a different limb phenotype through a different kind of lesion.

evidence.snippet: Brachydactyly type E (BDE; MIM#113300) is characterized by shortening of the metacarpal, metatarsal, and often phalangeal bones, and predominantly affects postaxial ray(s) of the limb.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the postaxial, metacarpal-and-metatarsal distribution of the lesion.

steps/2.description: The lesion acts on the metacarpal and metatarsal segments rather than on phalangeal segmentation, which is what separates type E from types A-C. Radiographs attribute the shortening to hypoplastic and partially fused metacarpal epiphyses, so as in type D the proximate abnormality is growth-plate behaviour in specific skeletal elements. Involvement is selective and asymmetric — most often the fourth ray, in variable combinations — and is postaxially weighted.

evidence.snippet: Short 4th metacarpal can be diagnosed by a positive metacarpal sign.

steps/3.description: The realised malformation: variable shortening of the metacarpals with phalanges of more or less normal length, terminal phalanges often short, metatarsals variably involved, hyperextensible hand joints, and mild short stature. The fourth metacarpal is the classic target and gives the metacarpal sign — a line touching the heads of the third and fifth metacarpals in the closed fist passes over, rather than through, the receding fourth.

steps/1.description: Mutations in NOTCH3, primarily missense mutations affecting cysteine residues in the extracellular EGF-like repeat domains, lead to abnormal NOTCH3 extracellular domain (ECD) multimerization and accumulation in small vessel walls. evidence.snippet: Granular osmiophilic material deposits around blood vessels are also a unique CADASIL feature and appear to have a role in sequestering proteins that are essential for blood vessel homeostasis.
evidence.explanation: This review confirms GOM deposits as a unique pathological feature of CADASIL that sequesters proteins important for vascular homeostasis.

evidence.snippet: The NOTCH3 R75Q mouse model showed pathological characteristics of CADASIL, with age-dependent NOTCH3ECD, granular osmiophilic material, and degenerated smooth muscle cells detected in the brain.

steps/2.description: Characteristic pathological deposits of granular osmiophilic material accumulate in the basement membrane of small arteries. GOM contains NOTCH3 extracellular domain fragments along with co-deposited extracellular matrix proteins including TIMP3 and vitronectin. evidence.snippet: Further proteomic and immunohistochemical analyses identified two functionally important extracellular matrix proteins, tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases 3 (TIMP3) and vitronectin (VTN) that are sequestered into Notch3(ECD)-containing aggregates.
evidence.explanation: Direct biochemical and immunohistochemical evidence that TIMP3 and vitronectin are sequestered into NOTCH3 ECD aggregates in CADASIL brain and artery samples, anchoring the matrisome co-aggregation mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Specifically, our results suggest a dysregulation of TIMP3 activity, which could contribute to mutant Notch3(ECD) toxicity by impairing extracellular matrix homeostasis in small vessels.
evidence.explanation: TIMP3 dysregulation, downstream of NOTCH3 ECD sequestration, impairs ECM homeostasis in cerebral small vessels, supporting the matrisome/proteostasis arm of CADASIL pathophysiology.

steps/3.description: Aggregating NOTCH3 ECD in CADASIL vessels abnormally recruits and sequesters matrisome proteins (TIMP3, vitronectin, LTBP1, clusterin), producing an HTRA1 loss-of-function profile in cerebral arterioles. Impaired ECM proteostasis amplifies vessel wall remodeling and biases the small artery phenotype toward fibrotic thickening with reduced matrix turnover.

evidence.snippet: We further found evidence for activation of the alternative pathway of complement. Immunolocalisation of complement Factor B, C3d and C5-9 terminal complex but not C1q was apparent in ~ 70% of cerebral vessels.

evidence.snippet: Functional VSMC cultures bearing the NOTCH3 Arg133Cys mutation showed increased gene expression of the pro-inflammatory cytokine interleukin 6 and ICAM-1 by 16- and 50-fold, respectively.

steps/5.description: Progressive thickening of arterial walls with loss of vascular smooth muscle cells leads to luminal narrowing, reduced cerebral blood flow, and chronic hypoperfusion of subcortical white matter. genes/0.notes: Autosomal dominant mutations in NOTCH3 cause CADASIL. Over 95% are missense mutations affecting cysteine residues in the 34 EGF-like repeat domains, leading to an odd number of cysteines and abnormal protein folding. Cysteine-sparing variants can also cause CADASIL-like pathology. Variant location within EGFr (EGF-like repeat) domains stratifies into three risk tiers: high-risk (HR-EGFr) domains include 1-6 plus 8, 11, and 26; medium-risk (MR-EGFr) and low-risk (LR-EGFr) cover the remaining domains. open_questions/0.rationale: Human neuroepithelial stem-cell knockdown establishes Golgi, spindle and nuclear abnormalities; patient fibroblasts show defective recycling and motility. The unresolved question is which of these routes causes specific human malformations or myelin loss. Patient-derived neural models with isogenic correction and developmental readouts could distinguish these contributions.

open_questions/1.rationale: The start-loss siblings have relatively preserved skills, yet one later regressed; skin-negative compound heterozygotes and variable keratoderma are documented. Protein mislocalization, residual translation and genetic background are distinguishable hypotheses. The mouse background effect demonstrates a model modifier effect, not a proven human modifier.

open_questions/2.rationale: The 2016 static LC3-II/p62/CHOP measurements were made in primary mouse fibroblasts and cannot distinguish induction from reduced clearance. Zebrafish and mouse ESCs show different marker responses, with a SNAP47-dependent effect in ESCs. Flux assays with appropriate turnover controls in patient keratinocytes and neural cells, alongside isogenic rescue, would test the contribution to human disease.

open_questions/3.rationale: Mixed-background mice survive with a functional neonatal barrier and no detectable cortical malformations. Zebrafish have a thinner periderm rather than hyperkeratosis. These divergences matter when selecting readouts for rescue experiments; neurological or skin improvement in one model does not demonstrate correction of the corresponding human mechanism.

evidence.snippet: an abnormal development of the embryonic ductal plate caused by genetically-determined dysfunctions of proteins expressed in the primary cilia of cholangiocytes
evidence.explanation: Places the fibrocystic liver diseases, Caroli disease among them, in the cholangiociliopathy class — the defect is in proteins of the cholangiocyte primary cilium.

evidence.snippet: a protein of unclear function, but supposedly involved in planar cell polarity and other fundamental cell functions
evidence.explanation: Links fibrocystin/polyductin to planar cell polarity, the process annotated on this node, but the source explicitly hedges ("unclear function", "supposedly"), so this is PARTIAL rather than SUPPORT.

evidence.snippet: In normal IBDUs, each cholangiocyte had a single cilium that expressed fibrocystin. In contrast, cilia in the PCK rat were abnormal with bulbous extensions and diminished length, and were devoid of fibrocystin.
evidence.explanation: The orthologous PCK rat Pkhd1 model demonstrates that fibrocystin is a cholangiocyte ciliary protein and that its loss produces the shortened, bulbous cilia described in this node.

steps/1.description: Biallelic PKHD1 variants reduce or abolish fibrocystin/polyductin, a large receptor-like protein that in normal biliary epithelium localises to the single primary cilium projecting from each cholangiocyte into the duct lumen. Loss of fibrocystin leaves the cilium structurally abnormal — shortened and with bulbous deformities — so the cholangiocyte can no longer transduce the ciliary signals that normally govern planar cell polarity and oriented growth of the developing duct. Because the same protein is required in renal tubular cilia, the biliary lesion is typically accompanied by the renal phenotype of autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease.

evidence.snippet: leading to biliary microhamartomas and segmental bile duct dilations. Biliary changes are accompanied by progressive deposition of abundant peribiliary fibrosis.
evidence.explanation: Describes the two consequences of the ductal dysgenesis modelled as the downstream edges of this node: segmental duct dilatation and peribiliary fibrosis.

steps/2.description: The intrahepatic bile ducts form from the ductal plate, a cylindrical sleeve of biliary precursors around each portal vein branch that is normally remodelled into tubular ducts during fetal life. In the fibrocystic liver diseases this remodelling fails, leaving persistent, abnormally shaped embryonic duct structures. Which level of the biliary tree is affected determines the clinical entity: dysgenesis of the small interlobular ducts produces congenital hepatic fibrosis, dysgenesis of the larger intrahepatic ducts produces Caroli disease, and involvement of both produces Caroli syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Caroli Disease (CD) and Caroli Syndrome (CS) are rare disorders presenting with dilation of the intrahepatic bile ducts.
evidence.explanation: Identifies intrahepatic bile duct dilatation as the defining presenting lesion of both forms.

evidence.snippet: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) and computed tomography (CT) examinations were most useful in diagnosing CD.
evidence.explanation: Supports the statement that the dilated ducts are demonstrated by MRCP and CT.

steps/3.description: The anatomical lesion that defines Caroli disease: multifocal, non-obstructive saccular or fusiform dilatations of the large intrahepatic ducts that remain in continuity with the biliary tree. Involvement may be confined to one segment or lobe or be diffuse and bilobar, and this distribution — not the histology — is what determines whether resection is feasible. The dilated segments are demonstrated non-invasively by MR cholangiopancreatography or CT.

evidence.snippet: the further progression of this destructive inflammatory state leads to recurrent episodes of cholangitis, the development of biliary stones and malignant transformation in some cases
evidence.explanation: Places biliary stone formation and recurrent cholangitis together as consequences of the ongoing destructive biliary process, supporting stasis within the dilated segments as their shared proximate step.

steps/4.description: Bile drains poorly from the saccular dilatations and stagnates within them. Stasis is the shared proximate cause of the two downstream complications: it supersaturates bile so that intrahepatic pigment stones form, and it permits ascending bacterial colonisation of the stagnant segments.

evidence.snippet: the further progression of this destructive inflammatory state leads to recurrent episodes of cholangitis, the development of biliary stones and malignant transformation in some cases
evidence.explanation: States directly that biliary stones develop as part of the disease course, the claim this node carries.

steps/5.description: Intrahepatic pigment stones form within the stagnant dilated segments. The stones are themselves obstructive, so they worsen the drainage failure that produced them and provide a nidus for bacterial colonisation, feeding the recurrent cholangitis.

evidence.snippet: Most patients had episodes of cholangitis, sepsis, fever or abdominal pain.
evidence.explanation: Across 561 pooled patients, cholangitis, sepsis, fever and abdominal pain were the dominant clinical events, supporting recurrent cholangitis as a core node.

evidence.snippet: Cholangitis is a major issue and necessitates anticipatory guidance and awareness.
evidence.explanation: A systematic review of 1,230 patients concludes that cholangitis is a major clinical problem in this disease group.

steps/6.description: Repeated ascending bacterial infection of the stagnant, stone-bearing segments produces the recurrent cholangitis that dominates the clinical course of the simple form — episodic fever, right upper quadrant pain and jaundice — and that can progress to biliary sepsis. Repeated infection also sustains the chronic inflammatory stimulus that underlies both the fibrotic and the neoplastic consequences below.

evidence.snippet: Due to focal inflammation, likely initiated by an intrauterine malformation of the bile ductal plate, the biliary tract is continuously destroyed over decades
evidence.explanation: Establishes sustained inflammatory destruction of the biliary tract over decades as the process this node describes.

steps/7.description: Decades of bile stasis and recurrent cholangitis expose the biliary epithelium to a sustained inflammatory and proliferative stimulus. The inflammatory state itself is well documented — it is the continuously destructive process that drives the clinical course — and it is separated here from the malignant transformation it is proposed to trigger, whose derivation is weaker.

evidence.snippet: Peribiliary fibrosis and biliary cysts are the fundamental lesions of FLDs and are responsible for the main clinical manifestations, such as portal hypertension, recurrent cholangitis, cholestasis, sepsis and eventually cholangiocarcinoma.
evidence.explanation: Names peribiliary fibrosis as one of the two fundamental lesions and links it directly to portal hypertension, the downstream node.

steps/8.description: Abundant fibrous tissue accumulates in the portal and periportal space around the malformed ducts. In Caroli syndrome this is the congenital hepatic fibrosis component and is developmental in origin, present from the outset rather than acquired; recurrent cholangitis adds a secondary inflammatory fibrogenic stimulus. The fibrosis is periportal and bridging rather than a true cirrhotic regenerative-nodule architecture, which is why hepatocellular synthetic function is characteristically preserved long after portal hypertension has become severe.

evidence.snippet: Depending on the size of the study population the incidence of cholangiocarcinoma varied from 2.7% to 37.5% with an overall incidence of 6.6%.
evidence.explanation: Provides the pooled cholangiocarcinoma incidence (6.6%) and the wide between-study range quoted in this node.

evidence.snippet: In 14 patients, CCA was found (Overall: 7,1%; CD: 6,3%, CS 7,6%).
evidence.explanation: An independent 198-patient multicentre series gives 7.1% overall, closely matching the pooled systematic-review estimate.

evidence.snippet: Tumor detection was an incidental finding of the surgical specimen in most cases because it is currently often impossible to detect tumor manifestation during preoperative diagnostics.
evidence.explanation: Supports the statement that malignancy is usually found incidentally in the resection specimen rather than preoperatively.

evidence.snippet: Twenty-one patients developed hepatobiliary cancer, with the majority having cholangiocarcinoma (n = 19).
evidence.explanation: Confirms cholangiocarcinoma as the dominant malignancy in this disease group.

steps/9.description: Cholangiocarcinoma arises at rates far above the general population. Age at diagnosis is nonetheless predominantly beyond 40 years (mean 60.1 years in Caroli syndrome and isolated congenital hepatic fibrosis), so the excess risk is one of incidence rather than of markedly earlier onset. Reported incidence varies widely between series — from under 3% to over a third in small cohorts — but the two largest systematic assessments converge on roughly 6-7%. Tumours are frequently found incidentally in the resection specimen because preoperative imaging cannot reliably distinguish malignancy from the underlying cystic architecture, and outcomes once malignancy is present are poor. The node is marked PROVISIONAL because the inflammation-to-carcinoma link is inferred from the epidemiological association and from the general biliary-inflammation carcinogenesis model rather than demonstrated directly in Caroli tissue.

evidence.snippet: At initial presentation in 2015, she had splenomegaly, severe esophagogastric fundal varices, preserved liver biochemistry, Child-Pugh class A disease, and a low model for end-stage liver disease score.
evidence.explanation: A worked single-patient example of the dissociation this node describes — severe portal hypertension (splenomegaly, fundal varices) with preserved liver biochemistry.

evidence.snippet: longitudinal follow-up showed persistent portal hypertension, recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding, and progressive impairment of hepatic reserve
evidence.explanation: Documents the decade-long erosion of hepatic reserve described in this node.

evidence.snippet: The nature of the portal hypertension was similar to that in other pediatric conditions (164 with varices, 74 bleeding varices, 81 underwent portosystemic shunting).
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the varices and variceal bleeding that constitute the clinical expression of portal hypertension in this disease group.

steps/10.description: Portal pressure rises because of the periportal fibrous obstruction, producing splenomegaly with hypersplenic cytopenias and portosystemic collaterals — principally oesophageal and gastric fundal varices that bleed recurrently. The presinusoidal site of obstruction explains the characteristic dissociation between severe portal hypertension and near-normal liver biochemistry early in the course. Over years, repeated decompensation and progressive cholestasis erode hepatic reserve, converting a compensated Child-Pugh class A patient into a transplant candidate.

edges/1.description: Loss of ciliary signalling in the developing biliary epithelium prevents normal remodelling of the embryonic ductal plate.

edges/2.description: Persistent unremodelled ductal plate segments of the large intrahepatic ducts present as the saccular dilatations that define Caroli disease.

edges/3.description: Ductal plate malformation of the small interlobular ducts is accompanied by deposition of dense peribiliary fibrous tissue — the congenital hepatic fibrosis component of Caroli syndrome.

edges/4.description: Bile pools within the saccular outpouchings, where it drains poorly from the dilated segments.

edges/5.description: Stagnant bile supersaturates and precipitates intrahepatic pigment stones within the dilated segments.

edges/6.description: Stagnant bile in segments that communicate with the biliary tree permits ascending bacterial colonisation and repeated infection.

edges/7.description: Intrahepatic stones further obstruct bile drainage and provide a nidus for bacterial colonisation, precipitating infective episodes.

edges/8.description: Repeated episodes of cholangitis maintain a chronic inflammatory microenvironment in the biliary epithelium.

edges/9.description: Recurrent biliary inflammation contributes to periportal fibrogenesis in addition to the developmental fibrosis of the ductal plate malformation.

edges/10.description: Periportal fibrous expansion obstructs portal venous inflow at a presinusoidal level, raising portal pressure while sinusoidal and hepatocellular function remain relatively spared.

evidence.snippet: As one trigger for the malignant transformation, chronic inflammation of the biliary epithelium during cholangitis with consecutive dysplasia and carcinogenesis is postulated
evidence.explanation: States the inflammation-to-carcinoma link explicitly, but as a postulated trigger rather than a demonstrated one — the reason the carcinoma node is graded PROVISIONAL.

edges/11.description: Chronic inflammation of the biliary epithelium with consecutive dysplasia is the postulated trigger for malignant transformation; the intervening steps are not established in Caroli tissue.

evidence.snippet: CHF, CD/CS, and ARPKD are caused by a number of mutations in polycystic kidney hepatic disease 1 (PKHD1), a gene that encodes for fibrocystin/polyductin
evidence.explanation: Directly attributes Caroli disease and Caroli syndrome, alongside congenital hepatic fibrosis and ARPKD, to PKHD1 mutations.

evidence.snippet: Our results indicate that fibrocystin is expressed in cholangiocyte cilia and that disruption of Pkhd1 by a germ line mutation in the PCK rat or by siRNA in IBDUs results in abnormalities in ciliary morphology and possibly biliary cystogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Orthologous rat model evidence that Pkhd1 disruption causes ciliary abnormalities and biliary cystogenesis.

genes/0.notes: PKHD1 encodes fibrocystin/polyductin, a cholangiocyte and renal tubular ciliary protein. Biallelic variants cause autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease together with the hepatic ductal plate malformation spectrum — congenital hepatic fibrosis, Caroli disease and Caroli syndrome. The protein's precise molecular function remains incompletely defined, with planar cell polarity the best-supported candidate role.

evidence.snippet: Cholangitis is a major issue and necessitates anticipatory guidance and awareness.
evidence.explanation: Establishes cholangitis as a major complication requiring active clinical management and anticipatory guidance.

treatments/0.description: Antimicrobial treatment of the recurrent bacterial cholangitis that arises from bile stasis, with anticipatory guidance for patients and families given how often infection recurs. Treatment is directed at the complication, not at the underlying ductal plate malformation.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Antimicrobials clear the bacterial infection of the stagnant biliary segments but do not correct the underlying stasis.

evidence.snippet: Symptoms improved after nonselective beta-blocker therapy; however, longitudinal follow-up showed persistent portal hypertension, recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding, and progressive impairment of hepatic reserve.
evidence.explanation: Single-patient evidence of initial symptomatic benefit followed by long-term failure to control portal hypertension — hence PARTIAL rather than SUPPORT.

treatments/1.description: Propranolol or carvedilol to lower portal pressure and reduce variceal bleeding risk. Symptomatically effective at first, but the reported long-term course shows persistent portal hypertension and recurrent bleeding despite therapy, including after conversion from propranolol to carvedilol.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Nonselective beta-blockade reduces portal inflow and portal pressure, the mechanism targeted for variceal bleeding prophylaxis.

evidence.snippet: she experienced recurrent hematemesis and melena despite sequential endoscopic variceal ligation and beta-blocker therapy
evidence.explanation: Documents recurrent bleeding despite sequential band ligation, supporting the described limitation of endoscopic therapy.

treatments/2.description: Endoscopic band ligation of bleeding oesophageal varices. Effective for acute haemorrhage control but, in the documented long-term course, did not prevent recurrent bleeding when applied sequentially over years.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Obliterates the variceal collaterals through which portal hypertension causes haemorrhage, without altering portal pressure itself.

evidence.snippet: There is risk of malignant transformation and patients with CD might also benefit from resection due to improvement of symptoms. Therefore, resection is strongly advised.
evidence.explanation: Multicentre surgical series concludes that resection is strongly advised, on grounds of both malignancy risk and symptom relief.

treatments/3.description: Segmental or lobar hepatectomy when the ductal dilatations are confined to a resectable part of the liver. Resection removes the stasis-and-infection focus, relieves symptoms, and eliminates the segment at risk of malignant transformation; occult cholangiocarcinoma is not infrequently found in the specimen.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Removes the malformed duct segments, eliminating the anatomical substrate for stasis, infection and carcinogenesis in the resected territory.

evidence.snippet: This case demonstrates the limitations of long-term endoscopic and pharmacological therapy in Caroli's disease complicated by portal hypertension and supports timely transplant referral before advanced hepatic decompensation occurs.
evidence.explanation: Supports transplantation as the definitive option and argues for timely referral, the recommendation captured in this treatment.

evidence.snippet: Interventional radiology or surgical treatments, including liver transplantation, are used in selected cases.
evidence.explanation: Confirms liver transplantation as an accepted treatment in selected cases of fibrocystic liver disease.

treatments/4.description: The definitive option for diffuse bilobar disease that cannot be resected, for hepatic decompensation, and for portal hypertension refractory to endoscopic and pharmacological therapy. Combined liver-kidney transplantation is considered when ARPKD has produced concurrent renal failure. Referral before advanced decompensation is advocated, since hepatic reserve declines progressively while complications recur.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: Replacing the fibrotic, malformed liver removes the presinusoidal obstruction and with it the portal hypertension.

evidence.snippet: Minimizing use of known nephrotoxic agents including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and aminoglycosides (unless otherwise advised) and of potentially hepatotoxic agents (e.g., acetaminophen doses >30 mg/kg/day, herbal supplements, and alcohol) is advised.
evidence.explanation: The GeneReviews Agents/Circumstances to Avoid guidance for ARPKD-PKHD1, recorded verbatim as the exposure-avoidance advice for the PKHD1-associated form of this entry.

treatments/5.description: Where Caroli disease occurs as the hepatobiliary presentation of ARPKD-PKHD1, GeneReviews advises minimising potentially hepatotoxic exposures — acetaminophen at doses above 30 mg/kg/day, herbal supplements and alcohol — alongside known nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs and aminoglycosides, on the rationale that hepatic and renal reserve are already committed by the underlying disease. Scope caveat: this guidance is written for ARPKD-PKHD1 and so applies to the PKHD1-associated Caroli syndrome form curated here; it should not be transferred wholesale to simple, frequently sporadic Caroli disease, whose genetic basis and renal involvement are not the same.

evidence.snippet: The development of intrahepatic carcinoma is described in both conditions, but the reported incidence varies extensively. Potential risk factors for the malignant transformation were not described.
evidence.explanation: States both halves of this knowledge gap explicitly — the incidence varies extensively and no risk factors for malignant transformation are known.

open_questions/0.rationale: Reported cholangiocarcinoma incidence ranges from 2.7% to 37.5% across studies, with pooled estimates of 6.6% (systematic review) and 7.1% (German multicentre series). All available series are retrospective and drawn from surgical cohorts, so they are subject to referral bias, and no predictor of malignant transformation has been identified. This matters clinically because malignancy risk is one of the arguments used to justify prophylactic resection, yet the tumours are almost always found incidentally in the specimen because preoperative imaging cannot detect them.

evidence.snippet: Targeted medical therapy is not available yet and thus the current treatment aims at controlling the complications.
evidence.explanation: States directly that no targeted medical therapy exists and that management is complication-directed.

open_questions/1.rationale: Every treatment curated in this entry acts on a consequence — infection, portal pressure, variceal bleeding, or the malformed anatomy itself — and none acts on the ciliary defect or on peribiliary fibrogenesis. A contributing obstacle is that fibrocystin/polyductin's molecular function is still not established, so there is no well-defined pathway to drug.

evidence.snippet: Artemis, DNA ligase IV, DNA protein kinase catalytic subunit, and Cernunnos/XLF genes in nonhomologous end joining pathways of DNA repair mechanisms have been identified as responsible for radiosensitive SCID.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports defective NHEJ DNA repair as the initiating disease mechanism in Cernunnos-XLF deficiency.

evidence.snippet: An increased cellular sensitivity to ionizing radiation, a defective V(D)J recombination, and an impaired DNA-end ligation process both in vivo and in vitro are indicative of a general DNA repair defect in these patients.
evidence.explanation: Patient-level demonstration of the three components of the repair defect - radiosensitivity, failed V(D)J recombination, and impaired DNA-end ligation - measured directly in affected individuals rather than inferred from the gene class.

evidence.snippet: Cernunnos/XLF represents a novel DNA repair factor essential for the NHEJ pathway.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the affected gene product is required for the NHEJ pathway itself.

steps/1.description: Cernunnos-XLF deficiency results from NHEJ1 dysfunction within the nonhomologous end joining DNA repair pathway, producing a radiosensitive DNA repair defect.

evidence.snippet: Here we review the mechanisms that repair programmed DNA lesions that occur during B-cell and T-cell development, as well as human diseases that arise through defects in these pathways.
evidence.explanation: This review supports the mechanistic link between NHEJ defects such as XLF deficiency and failed repair of programmed DNA breaks during B-cell and T-cell development.

steps/2.description: NHEJ pathway failure impairs repair of programmed DNA breaks during B-cell and T-cell development, producing combined immunodeficiency.

evidence.snippet: PURPOSE: We are reporting the first family from the Arabian Gulf with three siblings presenting with combined immunodeficiency (CID), microcephaly, and growth retardation due to a novel NHEJ1 splice site mutation, in addition to a review of the previously published literature on this subject.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports a distinct developmental-growth arm downstream of NHEJ1 deficiency.

steps/3.description: NHEJ1 deficiency causes a syndromic developmental phenotype with impaired growth and reduced brain growth in addition to immunodeficiency.

evidence.snippet: PURPOSE: We are reporting the first family from the Arabian Gulf with three siblings presenting with combined immunodeficiency (CID), microcephaly, and growth retardation due to a novel NHEJ1 splice site mutation, in addition to a review of the previously published literature on this subject.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports combined immunodeficiency as a core phenotype of NHEJ1-related Cernunnos-XLF deficiency.

steps/4.description: Combined immunodeficiency is a central clinical manifestation of Cernunnos-XLF deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Artemis, DNA ligase IV, DNA protein kinase catalytic subunit, and Cernunnos/XLF genes in nonhomologous end joining pathways of DNA repair mechanisms have been identified as responsible for radiosensitive SCID.
evidence.explanation: Places Cernunnos/XLF among the NHEJ genes responsible for radiosensitive SCID. This is a statement about the gene class rather than a measurement in patients, so the cellular radiosensitivity assay below carries the primary weight.

evidence.snippet: An increased cellular sensitivity to ionizing radiation, a defective V(D)J recombination, and an impaired DNA-end ligation process both in vivo and in vitro are indicative of a general DNA repair defect in these patients.
evidence.explanation: Increased cellular sensitivity to ionizing radiation measured directly in the five patients carrying Cernunnos mutations.

steps/5.description: Radiosensitivity is a cardinal feature of Cernunnos-XLF deficiency.

evidence.snippet: In conclusion, the patients with microcephaly, bird-like face, and severe growth retardation should be evaluated for hypogammaglobulinemia and primary immunodeficiency diseases.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports microcephaly as a characteristic syndrome feature.

steps/6.description: Microcephaly is a recurring syndromic feature in Cernunnos-XLF deficiency.

evidence.snippet: PURPOSE: We are reporting the first family from the Arabian Gulf with three siblings presenting with combined immunodeficiency (CID), microcephaly, and growth retardation due to a novel NHEJ1 splice site mutation, in addition to a review of the previously published literature on this subject.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports growth retardation as a core feature of the disease.

steps/7.description: Severe growth retardation is part of the syndromic phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Here we describe five patients with growth retardation, microcephaly, and immunodeficiency characterized by a profound T+B lymphocytopenia.
evidence.explanation: The original Cernunnos/XLF report identifies profound T+B lymphocytopenia in affected patients.

steps/8.description: T- and B-cell lymphocytopenia is a characteristic immune abnormality in Cernunnos-XLF deficiency.

evidence.snippet: The characteristic immune profile including a decrease in recent thymic emigrants and naive T cells, markedly elevated memory T cells together with normal to high IgM, and a decrease in IgG and IgA.
evidence.explanation: The Egyptian Cernunnos cohort reports decreased IgG and IgA as part of the characteristic immune profile.

steps/9.description: Decreased IgG and IgA can accompany the combined immunodeficiency profile.

evidence.snippet: The growth retarded and microcephalic boy with clinodactyly of both hands and hyperpigmentation of the skin suffered from recurrent respiratory infections.
evidence.explanation: This NHEJ1-deficient patient report directly documents recurrent respiratory infections.

steps/10.description: Recurrent respiratory infections are a clinical consequence of the combined immunodeficiency.

evidence.snippet: Cernunnos deficiency is a rare genetic disorder characterized by immunodeficiency, microcephaly, growth retardation, bird-like facies, sensitivity to ionizing radiation, few autoimmune manifestations, premature aging of hematopoietic stem cells at an early age, and occasional myeloproliferative disease.
evidence.explanation: This cohort abstract lists bird-like facies as a characteristic feature.

steps/11.description: Bird-like facies is part of the syndromic facial gestalt reported in Cernunnos-XLF deficiency.

edges/1.description: Failed DNA repair disrupts immune receptor rearrangement during lymphocyte maturation.

edges/2.description: Persistent DNA repair failure contributes to impaired somatic and brain growth.

edges/3.description: Failed lymphocyte receptor rearrangement compromises adaptive immune development.

edges/4.description: Impaired repair of DNA double-strand breaks causes increased sensitivity to ionizing radiation.

evidence.snippet: Here we describe five patients with growth retardation, microcephaly, and immunodeficiency characterized by a profound T+B lymphocytopenia.
evidence.explanation: The original Cernunnos/XLF report directly links the disease to profound T+B lymphocytopenia.

edges/5.description: Failed V(D)J recombination impairs T- and B-cell development, producing lymphocytopenia.

evidence.snippet: The characteristic immune profile including a decrease in recent thymic emigrants and naive T cells, markedly elevated memory T cells together with normal to high IgM, and a decrease in IgG and IgA.
evidence.explanation: The Egyptian Cernunnos cohort describes decreased IgG and IgA as part of the characteristic immune profile.

edges/6.description: Defective lymphocyte development can reduce circulating immunoglobulin concentrations, especially IgG and IgA.

evidence.snippet: The growth retarded and microcephalic boy with clinodactyly of both hands and hyperpigmentation of the skin suffered from recurrent respiratory infections.
evidence.explanation: This NHEJ1-deficient patient report directly documents recurrent respiratory infections.

edges/7.description: Combined immunodeficiency increases susceptibility to recurrent respiratory infections.

edges/8.description: Developmental DNA repair failure contributes to impaired brain growth.

edges/9.description: Systemic developmental impairment contributes to severe growth retardation.

evidence.snippet: Cernunnos deficiency is a rare genetic disorder characterized by immunodeficiency, microcephaly, growth retardation, bird-like facies, sensitivity to ionizing radiation, few autoimmune manifestations, premature aging of hematopoietic stem cells at an early age, and occasional myeloproliferative disease.
evidence.explanation: This cohort abstract lists bird-like facies as a characteristic feature of Cernunnos deficiency.

edges/10.description: Syndromic developmental consequences of NHEJ1 deficiency include the characteristic bird-like facial appearance.

evidence.snippet: Patients were found to have a homozygous splice site mutation immediately downstream of exon 3 in NHEJ1 (c.390 + 1G > C).
evidence.explanation: This directly supports NHEJ1 as the causal gene in Cernunnos-XLF deficiency.

evidence.snippet: Although both deletions were in-frame, immunoblotting did not reveal any NHEJ1 protein products in patient cells, indicating a null phenotype.
evidence.explanation: Functional demonstration that the allele is a protein-null despite producing in-frame transcripts, which is the basis for the loss-of-function assignment.

evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis revealed three different mutations in the NHEJ1 gene: a nonsense variant c.532C > T; p.(Arg178Ter), an intronic variant c.178-1G > A and a frameshift insertion variant c.233dup; p.(Asn78LysfsTer14).
evidence.explanation: Documents allelic heterogeneity - three distinct NHEJ1 variant classes across three families in a single cohort.

evidence.snippet: NHEJ1 | HGNC:25737 | Cernunnos-XLF deficiency | MONDO:0012650 | AR | Definitive
evidence.explanation: ClinGen classifies the NHEJ1-Cernunnos-XLF deficiency gene-disease relationship as definitive with autosomal recessive inheritance.

genes/0.notes: Cernunnos-XLF deficiency is caused by pathogenic NHEJ1 variants that can abolish detectable NHEJ1 protein and are typically inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern. The reported allelic spectrum is broad - nonsense, frameshift, splice-site and intronic variants have all been described - and an in-frame splice consequence does not predict a milder outcome, because in-frame exon skipping can still leave no detectable protein.

evidence.snippet: These patients received hematopoietic stem cells from HLA identical related donor without conditioning regimen and recovered without any complication.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports hematopoietic stem cell transplantation as an effective treatment option.

evidence.snippet: Now, both of the patients are well and alive seven and one yr after transplantation, respectively.
evidence.explanation: Durable post-transplant outcome, out to seven years in the longer-followed patient. This is the survival evidence behind treating HSCT as curative for the immune phenotype rather than only as engraftment.

evidence.snippet: A remarkable observation was the severe diarrhea that occurred in both patients soon after transplantation.
evidence.explanation: Supports the complication profile of the treatment rather than its efficacy: severe early post-transplant diarrhoea occurred in both patients and is a complication to anticipate, notwithstanding that the same report describes eventual recovery. Kept on this treatment entry so the adverse-course observation is not lost.

treatments/0.description: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation can provide curative treatment for the severe immunodeficiency component of the disease.

evidence.snippet: She is now on regular IVIG prophylaxis and has no new infection.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports immunoglobulin replacement as a supportive treatment for the immune phenotype.

treatments/1.description: Regular IVIG prophylaxis can reduce infection burden in affected individuals with antibody deficiency.

evidence.snippet: One pair of heterozygous missense mutations in the SET binding factor 1 (SBF1) gene (22q13.33), also called MTMR5, was identified as the underlying cause of the CMT4B family illness.
evidence.explanation: Establishes biallelic SBF1 variants as the causal lesion of the disease this entry curates.

evidence.snippet: The interacting protein was shown by mass spectrometry to be MTMR5, a catalytically inactive member of the MTM family.
evidence.explanation: The primary demonstration that MTMR5 is catalytically inactive - the fact that makes "loss of function" here mean loss of a regulatory role rather than loss of catalysis.

evidence.snippet: others lack key residues in the catalytic site and are classified as dead-phosphatases. However, these dead phosphatases regulate phosphoinositide-dependent cellular pathways by binding to catalytically active myotubularins.
evidence.explanation: A review of the myotubularin family stating the general mechanism this node applies to MTMR5: a dead phosphatase acts by binding an active one. Graded OTHER because the cited publication is a review rather than a study reporting its own data.

evidence.snippet: Functional analysis showed a markedly reduced level of MTMR5 protein encoded by SBF1 in the index case.
evidence.explanation: Direct protein-level demonstration that a pathogenic SBF1 allele reduces MTMR5, confirming the loss-of-function mechanism in patient material.

steps/1.description: Biallelic SBF1 variants - missense, frameshift or splice-site - reduce or abolish functional MTMR5. The protein's own myotubularin phosphatase domain is catalytically inactive, so this is not the loss of an enzyme. What is lost is MTMR5's regulatory and scaffolding role: a coiled-coil-mediated interaction that raises MTMR2's phosphoinositide 3-phosphatase activity and fixes where in the cell MTMR2 acts, and an N-terminal DENN domain that activates Rab GTPases. Reported pathogenic variants cluster in the DENN and SBF2 domains but occur throughout the gene, and are generally associated with loss of expression or of function. A frameshift allele has been shown directly to reduce MTMR5 protein in patient cells. `zygosity` is deliberately left unset: reported families are homozygous (the consanguineous ones) or compound heterozygous (the index Korean and the Italian families), the slot is single-valued, and the enum has no "biallelic" value that would cover both without misreporting one.

evidence.snippet: Through this interaction, MTMR5 increases the enzymatic activity of MTMR2 and dictates its subcellular localization.
evidence.explanation: The two functions of MTMR5 that are lost - activation of MTMR2 and control of its localization - which is exactly what this node claims.

evidence.snippet: We also demonstrate that MTMR2 interacts with MTMR5 via its coiled-coil domain and that mutations in the coiled-coil domain of either MTMR2 or MTMR5 abrogate this interaction.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the coiled-coil interface this node names, and shows that mutation of it abolishes the interaction.

evidence.snippet: While some members have phosphatase activity against the 3-phosphate of phosphoinositides, regulating the phosphorylation status of PtdIns3P and PtdIns(3,5)P2 implicated in membrane trafficking and autophagy, and producing PtdIns5P
evidence.explanation: Names the two phosphoinositide species whose handling this node says is misregulated - PtdIns3P and PtdIns(3,5)P2 - and ties them to membrane trafficking. Graded OTHER as a review statement rather than primary data.

evidence.snippet: In the mouse PNS, Mtmr2 was required to maintain wild-type levels of Mtmr5 and Mtmr13, suggesting that these factors function in discrete protein complexes.
evidence.explanation: Shows the partnering is mutually stabilizing in vivo, so losing one member of the complex is not a one-way effect on the other.

steps/2.description: MTMR5 binds MTMR2 through its coiled-coil domain, increases MTMR2's enzymatic activity and dictates where MTMR2 is localized. Without that partnering, dephosphorylation of the endosomal phosphoinositides PI3P and PI(3,5)P2 is misregulated in both amount and place. Because MTMR5 has no catalytic activity of its own, this is the step at which a pseudophosphatase lesion becomes a phosphoinositide lesion.

evidence.snippet: β1-integrin through early endosomes is controlled by Rab21, which the DENN domain of Mtmr5/13 has been shown to activate
evidence.explanation: Names a specific cargo and the Rab that routes it, connecting the DENN domain lost in CMT4B3 to a concrete trafficking step in Schwann cells.

evidence.snippet: β1-integrin is required for the extension and maintenance of Schwann cell processes around axons; loss of this surface receptor leads to radial sorting defects and delayed myelination in mice
evidence.explanation: Supplies the reason a trafficking defect reaches radial sorting: the receptor whose routing depends on Rab21 is the one Schwann cells need to extend processes around axons.

evidence.snippet: Although almost ubiquitously expressed, pathogenic variants primarily impact on the peripheral nervous system, corroborating the involvement of MTMR5/SBF1 and its molecular partners in Schwann cells-mediated myelinization.
evidence.explanation: States the tissue-selectivity argument this node makes: broad expression, peripheral-nerve-selective disease, implicating Schwann-cell myelination.

evidence.snippet: MTMR5/SBF1 is a pseudophosphatase predicted to regulate endo-lysosomal trafficking in tandem with other MTMRs.
evidence.explanation: Names the cellular process this node is about and its dependence on other myotubularins.

steps/3.description: Schwann cells are unusually sensitive to disruption of endolysosomal membrane trafficking - nearly half the CMT4 genes encode regulators of that pathway - because building and maintaining the myelin sheath requires large, precisely directed membrane flux and correct trafficking of the receptors that time myelination. MTMR5 is almost ubiquitously expressed, yet SBF1 variants strike the peripheral nervous system, which is the observation this node explains.

evidence.snippet: Studies in muscle identified partial defects of oxidative metabolism.
evidence.explanation: The in-patient observation that the mitochondrial arm of this node rests on.

evidence.snippet: CMT4B3 fibroblasts showed normal basal macroautophagy but failed to increase autophagy in response to mitochondrial stress or protein aggregates. Conversely, mitophagy was strongly activated via the PINK1-PRKN pathway.
evidence.explanation: The autophagic-selectivity result this node names, measured in patient-derived fibroblasts.

evidence.snippet: Patient fibroblasts exhibited fragmented mitochondrial networks with a shift toward fission, together with reduced ATP production, while mitochondrial mass, respiratory chain assembly, and markers of mitochondrial biogenesis were preserved.
evidence.explanation: Preserved respiratory chain assembly alongside reduced ATP output is the specific observation supporting "secondary" rather than primary mitochondrial disease.

steps/4.description: Muscle from one CMT4B3 child showed partial defects of oxidative metabolism, and fibroblasts from the same patient have fragmented mitochondrial networks with reduced ATP production despite preserved mitochondrial mass and respiratory chain assembly, strongly activated PINK1-PRKN mitophagy without the matching rise in macroautophagy, and features of premature senescence. This is presented as a downstream consequence of the trafficking and autophagy lesion, not as a primary respiratory chain defect - which is what separates CMT4B3 from CMT4K, where the gene itself is a complex IV assembly factor.

evidence.snippet: We found a similar loss of large myelinated fibers and focally folded myelin sheaths in our patients, but the actual number of myelinated fibers was different from CMT4B1 and CMT4B2.
evidence.explanation: Documents both halves of this node in CMT4B3 nerve biopsies, and the one quantitative difference from the sibling diseases.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in these genes can lead to focal myelin out-folding and secondary axonal loss in peripheral nerves
evidence.explanation: Restates the outfolding-to-axonal-loss sequence for the CMT4B group (MTMR2, SBF2 and SBF1) that this node and the next but one assert.

steps/5.description: The histological signature of the CMT4B group: myelin sheaths that fold back on themselves into redundant loops and outfoldings, with loss of large myelinated fibers. In CMT4B3 this was found in the index Korean family, although the absolute number of myelinated fibers differed from CMT4B1 and CMT4B2. It is characteristic of the demyelinating presentation and is not reported in the axonal syndromic families.

evidence.snippet: Loss of Mtmr5 in mice did not cause CMT4B-like myelin outfoldings. However, adult Mtmr5-/- mouse nerves contained fewer myelinated axons than control nerves, likely as a result of axon radial sorting defects.
evidence.explanation: The primary evidence for this node, and simultaneously the negative result that the mouse does not reproduce the human outfolding pathology.

evidence.snippet: Consistently, Mtmr5 levels were highest during axon radial sorting and fell sharply after postnatal day seven.
evidence.explanation: Developmental expression timing consistent with a radial-sorting role rather than an ongoing myelin-maintenance one.

steps/6.description: Radial sorting is the developmental step in which Schwann cells segregate large-calibre axons out of bundles into 1:1 relationships before myelinating them. Mouse work places MTMR5's main peripheral-nerve role here rather than in myelin maintenance: Mtmr5-null nerves contain fewer myelinated axons and show sorting defects, while Mtmr13 loss produces the outfoldings. Whether this division of labour holds in human CMT4B3, where outfoldings are seen, is unresolved - see the model-mismatch discussion below.

evidence.snippet: These changes are accompanied at the pathological level by abnormal axon outgrowths and by the presence of dysmyelination changes reminiscent of the nerve pathology in human Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4B3.
evidence.explanation: Model-organism support that mtmr5 loss is sufficient to produce dysmyelination resembling the human lesion.

evidence.snippet: In contrast to CMT4B1, CMT4B2, and the pure neuropathic form of CMT4B3, which are all characterized by demyelinating neuropathy with focally folded myelin sheaths, both families presented a predominantly axonal sensory motor neuropathy
evidence.explanation: Records the split this node describes between the demyelinating and axonal electrophysiological patterns within SBF1 disease.

steps/7.description: The structurally abnormal sheath conducts badly. In the demyelinating presentation this appears as markedly slowed motor conduction velocities; in the axonal syndromic presentation velocities are relatively preserved and it is the action-potential amplitudes that collapse. A zebrafish mtmr5 knockout shows dysmyelination changes described as reminiscent of the human nerve pathology.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in these genes can lead to focal myelin out-folding and secondary axonal loss in peripheral nerves
evidence.explanation: States the outfolding-to-secondary-axonal-loss sequence that this node is the endpoint of.

evidence.snippet: We found a similar loss of large myelinated fibers and focally folded myelin sheaths in our patients
evidence.explanation: Loss of large myelinated fibers on CMT4B3 sural nerve biopsy is the histological expression of this node.

steps/8.description: Length-dependent loss of peripheral axons follows the myelin lesion and is what tracks disability. It is the shared endpoint of the demyelinating and axonal presentations, and drives the distal-predominant motor and sensory deficit and the foot deformity.

evidence.snippet: Four siblings of consanguineous Bedouin kindred presented at infancy with an autosomal recessive syndrome of congenital microcephaly, facial dysmorphism, strabismus, developmental delay and ataxia with positive pyramidal signs.
evidence.explanation: Documents the CNS arm of this node - microcephaly, developmental delay, ataxia and pyramidal signs - in a family with a null SBF1 allele.

evidence.snippet: Of note, both mutations causative of syndromic CMT4B3 fall within the DENN domain
evidence.explanation: Supports the genotype argument this node makes for why the syndromic families differ, without asserting the mechanism.

evidence.snippet: starting by 10 days post-fertilization, mutant zebrafish develop obvious morphometric changes in head size and brain volume
evidence.explanation: Model-organism support that mtmr5 loss alone can produce a brain-size phenotype, consistent with a CNS role for MTMR5.

evidence.snippet: In total, these data demonstrate that the microcephaly phenotype in mtmr5-KO zebrafish is not caused by excessive apoptosis, autophagy or cell loss in the nervous system, indicating instead potential defects in early neurogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Constrains the CNS mechanism in the one model that shows it: a neurodevelopmental defect rather than degeneration. Zebrafish, so it is a lead for the human CNS arm, not an account of it.

steps/9.description: In the syndromic families, SBF1 loss also produces progressive microcephaly, intellectual disability, cerebellar atrophy with ataxia and pyramidal signs, and degeneration of multiple cranial nerves. The mechanism is not established. Two observations argue that it is not simply more of the same Schwann-cell lesion: the syndromic variants fall in the DENN domain, which only SBF1 and SBF2 carry among the myotubularins, and the mtmr5-null zebrafish develops reduced head size and brain volume rather than a purely peripheral phenotype. Not every severe case has it - one child with severe infantile axonal disease had normal brain MRI and normal cognition throughout.

evidence.snippet: All patients had onset of distal atrophy and weakness in upper and lower limbs, decreased vibration and position sense, areflexia, and pes planus in the first decade, with a slow progression to loss of ambulation in the fifth decade of life.
evidence.explanation: Documents distal weakness and atrophy in all affected members of the index family, with first-decade onset.

evidence.snippet: they developed areflexia, multiple cranial neuropathies and severe polyneuropathy with progressive muscle weakness, affecting proximal and distal extremities
evidence.explanation: Shows that in the syndromic form the weakness is severe and not confined to distal muscles.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals have the typical CMT phenotype of distal muscle weakness and atrophy associated with sensory loss and, frequently, pes cavus foot deformity.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews names distal muscle weakness and atrophy as the typical phenotype of the CMT4 series. Indirect because the statement is made of the whole autosomal recessive CMT4 group, in which SBF1/CMT4B3 is one of eleven genes, rather than of CMT4B3 specifically.

steps/10.description: Length-dependent weakness and wasting of the distal upper and lower limbs, beginning in the first decade in the classic form and in infancy or early childhood in the severe forms. The syndromic families also show proximal involvement.

evidence.snippet: decreased vibration and position sense, areflexia, and pes planus in the first decade
evidence.explanation: Documents impaired vibration and position sense in the index CMT4B3 family.

evidence.snippet: no clinical and neurophysiological evidences of distal sensory impairment
evidence.explanation: A reported CMT4B3 patient in whom distal sensory impairment was absent on both clinical and neurophysiological assessment, so sensory loss is not an obligate feature of this disease. Scoped to the classic subtype.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals have the typical CMT phenotype of distal muscle weakness and atrophy associated with sensory loss and, frequently, pes cavus foot deformity.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews names sensory loss as part of the typical CMT4 phenotype. Indirect because the statement is made of the whole autosomal recessive CMT4 group rather than of CMT4B3, and it sits alongside the REFUTE item above from a CMT4B3 family in whom sensory involvement was absent.

steps/11.description: Impaired vibration and joint position sense distally in the classic demyelinating form. Sensory involvement is variable across the spectrum: it was largely spared in the Syrian "fork and bracket" siblings, and the Italian child with severe infantile axonal disease had no clinical or neurophysiological distal sensory impairment.

evidence.snippet: Toward the end of their first decade, they developed areflexia, multiple cranial neuropathies and severe polyneuropathy with progressive muscle weakness
evidence.explanation: Documents areflexia in the Bedouin syndromic family.

steps/12.description: Loss of deep tendon reflexes, present across both the classic and the syndromic presentations.

evidence.snippet: Physical assessment exhibited kyphoscoliosis, bilateral syndactyly and distal muscle wasting with drop-foot and pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: Documents pes cavus and drop-foot in a CMT4B3 family.

evidence.snippet: There was distal muscle wasting and weakness but no pes cavus.
evidence.explanation: Records a CMT4B3 family with distal wasting but no pes cavus, so foot deformity is not present in every affected individual.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals have the typical CMT phenotype of distal muscle weakness and atrophy associated with sensory loss and, frequently, pes cavus foot deformity.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews states that pes cavus is frequently but not invariably present in the CMT4 series, which is the only frequency statement any source makes about foot deformity in this disease group. Indirect because it describes the CMT4 group rather than CMT4B3, and it is drawn from a chapter GeneReviews has retired.
